text.p: **BIRTHDAYS**
English seaman WILLIAM BLIGH, who faced a mutinous crew on the "Bounty", was born in 1754. As governor of New South Wales, he was deposed by locals who wanted to use rum as currency.
English/Australian shipbuilder JOHN KORFF was born in 1799. He was denied a place in history when KORFF's HARBOUR was resurveyed as COFFS HARBOUR.
Australian cricketer FREDERICK SPOFFORTH was born in 1853. He was nicknamed "the demon" for his fast bowling action.
Australian conservative Prime Minister SIR JOHN GREY GORTON was born in 1911. In retirement he made whisky advertisements and became a patron for the "legalise marihuana" lobby group.
American singer/songwriter OTIS REDDING, known for "Try A Little Tenderness" and "Sittin' On The Dock Of The Bay", was born in 1941.
British world-class ice-skating star JOHN CURRY, who won the European men's single title, the winter olympics gold medal and the world championships in Stockholm, was born in 1949.

UK guitarist, pianist and songwriter of the 'Eurythmics' DAVID A. STEWART was born in 1952. In 1977 he formed the groups "Tourists' with ANNIE LENNOX and from 1981 the pair joined up in the 'Eurythmics'. "Love Is A Stranger" (1982), "Sweet Dreams (Are Made Of This)" (1983), "Who's That Girl" (1983), "Thorn In My Side" (1986) and a "Sisters Are Doin It For Themselves" (1985).
** EVENTS **
1835 : The British Municipal Corporations Act reformed
urban government, bringing about a system of local government.
1901 : Post-impressionist artist HENRI DE

TOULOUSE-LAUTREC died following a paralytic stroke, brought on by syphilis and alcoholism. Born an aristocrat, he smashed both thighs in a fall from a horse when he was 14, and resulting bone-disease left him stunted.
1911 : The first airmail service began in Britain between
Hendon and Windsor.
1946 : TAA began operations as an Australian airline.
Its first service was a daily passenger flight between Sydney and Melbourne.
1948 : North Korea proclaimed its independence.
1952 : Australian Prime Minister ROBERT MENZIES gave
Cabinet a report, detailing known and suspected communists in the public service.
1958 : Those reponsible for Britain's Notting Hill race

riots were jailed, and the magistrate condemned the media for its part in the three days of destruction. More than 150 people were arrested and hundreds were injured in the north London riots. Police said it started when extreme right-wing activists attacked five blacks. The riots involved petrol bombings and street battles between gangs of up to 2,000. A television director was accused of starting another riot by reconstructing a previous clash between blacks and whites.
1976 : The revered chairman MAO of China died at the age
of 82 after a series of strokes. In 1949, MAO TSE-TUNG's communist army overthrew the nationalist forces of CHIANG KAI-SHEK and established the People's Republic of China.
1978 : An 18-year-old Czech tennis player defected.
MARTINA NAVRATILOVA asked the United States for politicial asylum.
1988 : Australians voted against four-year Parliamentary
terms in a referendum.
1991 : An Israeli teenager showed detectives how he had

hacked into the Pentagon computers to find out how the top-secret Patriot anti-missiles worked. Eighteen-year-old DERI SCHRIEBMAN's undoing was when he tired of browsing through military secrets, and turned to the Visa credit card computer system. He then provided the details to an international network of teenage hackers who went on a spending spree. Six were arrested in the United States and Canada. DERI also showed the investigators how he could make free long-distance telephone calls.
1994 : A US-Air 737 airliner crashed in Pennysylvania,
killing all 131 people on board.
